question: Which durable memory-core dreaming scoping API should OpenClaw support for multi-agent installs: plugin-level dreaming.agents allowlist, agents.list[].dreaming overrides, per-agent/staggered schedules, or pressure/backoff without explicit scoping?
rationale: The current behavior is source-proven, but the fix creates a strict user config contract and the open candidate PRs use different API shapes; repository policy requires maintainer intent before adding or choosing that surface.

options.title: Plugin-level allowlist first
options.body: Add a memory-core-owned dreaming.agents allowlist for the minimum durable scoping need, keeping per-agent schedules and pressure backoff as follow-up decisions.

options.title: Per-agent dreaming block
options.body: Add agents.list[].dreaming as the user-facing override surface, accepting a broader core agent config contract tied to a plugin-owned behavior.

options.title: Scheduler/backoff only
options.body: Address peak memory with stagger or pressure-based deferral but leave explicit opt-out for non-consuming agents unresolved.

recommendation.title: Plugin-level allowlist first
recommendation.body: Add a memory-core-owned dreaming.agents allowlist for the minimum durable scoping need, keeping per-agent schedules and pressure backoff as follow-up decisions.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has recent history across the memory dreaming resolver/runtime/docs surface and is the strongest routing candidate for the config/API direction decision.
